mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the cost of capital and increase equity valuations. This relationship holds without threshold conditions.
evidence_refs: fact:Current FEDFUNDS at 0.79% is historically low
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return correlation with FEDFUNDS is non-negative (r >= 0) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals a tightening labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE falls below 4.5% (based on 2010-2017 data).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in labor market strength (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL above 2.5%) signals an overheating economy, prompting the Fed to tighten policy and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS MoM > 0.5% and INDPRO MoM > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 2.5%
failure_condition: The interaction of PAYEMS, INDPRO, and CPIAUCSL does not produce negative returns in more than 55% of triggered instances (2010-2017 data).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 1.0% for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced corporate borrowing.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 1.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during a monetary tightening cycle (2010-2017 data).

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and 20-day S&P 500 returns is non-positive (r <= 0) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 200,000 jobs per month, it signals a robust labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong economic activity, but if the growth rate of INDPRO exceeds that of RSAFS, it may signal supply chain bottlenecks and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of INDPRO and RSAFS does not produce negative returns in more than 55% of triggered instances (2010-2017 data).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion characterized by high housing starts (HOUST > 1300 thousand units), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days as the housing market peaks and consumer spending moderates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle expansion (2010-2017 data).
